feed.description: Recurring guests from other shows revisit their positions.
feed.title: Cross-Show

bullets: Two years of systems-thinking work breeds humility about leverage points rather than confidence in them — a lesson observed at teams using Bloomberg and IPCC.
Ignoring the lessons of leverage points leads to rebuilding from scratch a year later; internalizing them makes the rest of the decisions easier.
Reliability and sustainability share more vocabulary than is commonly admitted — their overlap is where systems thinking intersects with sustainability work.
The second-order effect is the part most people miss, and it deserves attention over first-order outcomes.
Trade-offs around reliability cross-cut every other theme in systems thinking rather than standing as an isolated concern.
Running one idea for two weeks offers a practical starting point — the rest is iteration rather than upfront perfection.
